draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Bekal Fort! This is the biggest fort in Kerala, a huge circle of laterite walls standing right in the sea. It was built in the 1600s by the Keladi Nayakas.
draft.hungryLine: Kasaragod cooking mixes Kerala and Karnataka. Try fish curry and rice dumplings.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk the walls all the way round, then climb the observation tower.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit on the walls facing the sea and wait for the sunset.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The song 'Uyire' from the film Bombay was shot right here, on these walls in the rain.

legends.title: Holes for spying
legends.body: Look closely at the walls. They're full of small holes, angled so defenders could fire at ships on the sea and the shore.

legends.title: A temple at the door
legends.body: A Hanuman temple stands at the fort's entrance, and an old mosque from Tipu Sultan's time is nearby.

tips.title: Late afternoon is best.
tips.body: The heat drops and the sunset lights up the walls.

tips.title: Keep your ticket.
tips.body: You may need it to re-enter after a walk on the beach.

story.title: The Nayakas build
story.body: Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi built the fort to guard this stretch of coast.

story.title: Tipu Sultan
story.body: Tipu Sultan took Bekal as he pushed into Malabar, and used it as a base.

story.title: The British arrive
story.body: After Tipu's defeat, the East India Company took over the fort.

story.title: A film star
story.body: The rain song in Mani Ratnam's film Bombay made Bekal famous all over India.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Walk the walls, climb the tower, then watch the sunset from the beach. Tell me what you could see from the top.
